status_summary: An interim final rule published 2025-07-31 delayed the Super Emitter Program implementation deadline to 2027-01-22, and a final rule published and effective 2025-12-03 kept that date, citing unanticipated difficulties in implementing the novel program. On 2026-10-29 EPA published a proposed rule (91 FR 68234, docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0163) to rescind the Super Emitter Program, which lets third parties report large methane releases that operators must investigate, in the oil and gas new source standards and existing source guidelines, with comments due 2026-12-16. The proposal is not final, so the program's 2027-01-22 start date and obligations remain in the codified rules unless EPA finalizes the rescission or extends the date again.

timeline.event: EPA published an interim final rule extending oil and gas methane rule deadlines, including delaying the Super Emitter Program implementation deadline to 2027-01-22.
EPA finalized the deadline extensions, keeping the Super Emitter Program start at 2027-01-22.

EPA published a proposed rule (91 FR 68234, FR Doc. 2026-22082; docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0163; RIN 2060-AW73; 40 CFR part 60) to rescind the Super Emitter Program in NSPS OOOO, OOOOa and OOOOb and emissions guidelines OOOOc, including the third-party certification and notification provisions and source response obligations, citing insufficient evidence on super-emitter events, other requirements expected to address most such events, over-breadth, and inadequate statutory bases for the program; it also co-proposes subcategorizing well sites (marginal and non-marginal, or conventional and non-conventional). Comments are due 2026-12-16.
